brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent hex base pieces (piece at 0,0,0 and 1,0,0) carry the holder; capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2, two full-depth bins with 2 compartments each, no drain holes so they hold utensils rather than letting them drain.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only and has no waterproofing check. Waterproofing depends on the material and print settings the user chooses; the build uses solid bins and caps with no drain or pill/radial holes, but that is not verified as waterproof.
Dishwasher safety depends on material (heat and detergent resistance), which the configurator does not model. Not verified; the user must choose a dishwasher-safe material.

finish.summary: Built a utensil holder: two hex base cells with two full-depth, two-compartment bins, open faces capped and joints locked. The fit check is clear. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe are material properties the configurator cannot verify, so they are reported unmet; the user needs to pick a suitable material (e.g., one rated for dishwasher use) and confirm sealing separately.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
